audit_status.source_base: Hebrew 2 Kings / Melakhim Bet Naaman, captive girl, Elisha, Jordan washing, and Gehazi narrative, draft aligned later
audit_status.review_note: First-pass draft reviewed for Naaman's military status and skin disease, the unnamed captive Israelite girl's agency, diplomatic misreading, Elisha's refusal of spectacle, Jordan washing, anti-xenophobia, Gehazi's deception and wealth-taking, and disease transfer language.

verses.restored: Naaman, commander of army of king of Aram, was a great man before his lord and lifted of face, because by him YHWH had given victory to Aram. The man was a mighty man of strength, and afflicted with a skin disease.
Arameans had gone out in raiding bands and captured from land of Israel a young girl, and she was before Naaman's wife.
She said to her mistress, If only my lord were before prophet who is in Samaria, then he would gather/heal him from his skin disease.
He went and told his lord, saying, Thus and thus spoke the girl who is from land of Israel.
King of Aram said, Go, enter, and I will send a letter to king of Israel. He went and took in his hand ten talents of silver, six thousand gold pieces, and ten changes of garments.
He brought letter to king of Israel, saying, Now when this letter comes to you, look, I have sent to you Naaman my servant so you may gather/heal him from his skin disease.

It was, when king of Israel read the letter, that he tore his garments and said, Am I Divine, to put to death and make alive, that this one sends to me to gather/heal a man from his skin disease? Surely know and see that he seeks occasion against me.

It was, when Elisha man of Divine heard that king of Israel tore his garments, that he sent to king, saying, Why have you torn your garments? Let him come now to me, and he shall know there is a prophet in Israel.
Naaman came with his horses and chariot and stood at entrance of house of Elisha.
Elisha sent a messenger to him, saying, Go and wash seven times in Jordan, and your flesh shall return to you, and you shall be clean.

Naaman was angry and went away, saying, Look, I said to myself, Going out, he will surely come out to me, stand, call in name of YHWH his Divine, wave his hand over place, and gather/heal the skin disease.
Are not Abanah and Pharpar, rivers of Damascus, better than all waters of Israel? Could I not wash in them and be clean? He turned and went in fury.
His servants drew near and spoke to him, saying, My father, had prophet spoken to you a great thing, would you not do it? How much more when he said to you, Wash and be clean?
He went down and dipped in Jordan seven times according to word of man of Divine, and his flesh returned like flesh of a little boy, and he was clean.

He returned to man of Divine, he and all his camp, came and stood before him, and said, Look, now I know there is no Divine in all earth except in Israel. Now please take a blessing/gift from your servant.
He said, As YHWH lives, before whom I stand, I will not take. He pressed him to take, but he refused.
Naaman said, If not, please let there be given to your servant burden of a pair of mules of earth, for your servant will no longer make burnt offering or sacrifice to other gods, but to YHWH.

For this thing may YHWH forgive your servant: when my lord enters house of Rimmon to bow there, and he leans upon my hand, and I bow in house of Rimmon—when I bow in house of Rimmon, may YHWH forgive your servant in this thing.
He said to him, Go in peace. He went from him a short distance.
Gehazi, servant of Elisha man of Divine, said, Look, my lord spared Naaman this Aramean by not taking from his hand what he brought. As YHWH lives, I will run after him and take something from him.
Gehazi pursued after Naaman. Naaman saw one running after him, fell from chariot to meet him, and said, Is it peace?
He said, Peace. My lord sent me, saying, Look, just now two young men from sons of prophets came to me from hill country of Ephraim. Please give them one talent of silver and two changes of garments.
Naaman said, Be willing, take two talents. He urged him and bound two talents of silver in two bags, with two changes of garments, and gave them to two of his young men, and they carried before him.
He came to hill/Ophel, took from their hand, deposited in house, and sent men away, and they went.
He entered and stood before his lord. Elisha said to him, From where, Gehazi? He said, Your servant did not go here or there.
He said to him, Did not my heart go when man turned from upon his chariot to meet you? Is it time to take silver and garments, olive groves and vineyards, sheep and cattle, male and female servants?
Skin disease of Naaman shall cling to you and to your seed forever. He went out from before him afflicted with skin disease, white as snow.

translation_notes: Naaman is both an honored military commander and a person with a skin disease. Disease does not erase dignity, competence, or personhood.
The unnamed Israelite girl is a captive taken in a raid. Her insight drives the entire healing narrative, but her enslavement and displacement must not disappear behind Naaman's cure.
The Hebrew tsara'at does not equal modern leprosy/Hansen's disease by default. Use 'skin disease' pending fuller medical-historical audit and avoid contagion stigma.
YHWH giving victory to Aram complicates nationalist theology and prevents assuming Divine action belongs only to Israel's military interests.
The king misreads the letter as a diplomatic provocation, showing how illness and healing can be politicized by rulers.
Elisha refuses wealth and spectacle; healing is not sold, and prophetic authority is not validated by performance theatrics.
Naaman's servants successfully challenge his pride. Subordinates can offer wise correction without being devalued.
Naaman's request for Israelite earth reflects ancient territorial theology. His continued state duty in Rimmon's temple is met with 'Go in peace,' not coercive purity policing.
Gehazi exploits a healed foreigner through lies and invented charitable need. Religious workers may not monetize access, fabricate need, or use vulnerable people's gratitude.
The transfer of skin disease to Gehazi and his descendants is morally dangerous collective-punishment language and must not be used to explain illness, heredity, disability, or family suffering.
safety_note: Do not stigmatize skin disease, disability, foreigners, captives, servants, or interfaith complexity. Do not erase the captive girl's trauma or use Naaman's healing to glorify war. Healing is not for sale. Gehazi's punishment language may not justify disease blame, inherited guilt, or shaming families.
